items.claim: The superscription row's Hebrew claims all reach byte tier and its verse-initial dibrey exclusivity digit is byte-true, with the header-vs-genitive hazard correctly navigated.
items.evidence: Both quoted runs re-collate at byte tier against their cited ref: דִּבְרֵי֙ קֹהֶ֣לֶת and בֶּן דָּוִ֔ד מֶ֖לֶךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם (oshb:Eccl.1.1). The exclusivity digit checks out against consonantal_index.json directly: verse-initial dibrey stands at exactly 4 verses (Eccl.1.1, Eccl.9.17, Eccl.10.12, Eccl.12.11), and the other three open genitive phrases (dibrey-chakhamim at 9:17 and 12:11, dibrey-pi-chakham at 10:12) rather than headers, which is what the row asserts. The row did not reach for the inflated figure available here: a bare contiguous-skeleton sweep of dibrey returns 14 verses (it catches ha-devarim at 1:8 and kindred forms), so the 4-verse digit is the correctly word-bound one and the swept object is named. The device note is byte-true by absence against two digit-bearing inventories: MT 1:1 appears in neither the bare hevel token hit-list (sweep: 30 verses) nor the tachat-hashemesh hit-list (sweep: 27 verses). Nothing is owed on the disclosure side either: pmarks_Eccl.json places no PE, no SAMEKH, no paseq and no ketiv/qere note at MT 1:1, and the row asserts no mark. No maqaf is asserted in either quoted run, correct for this maqaf-free extract.

items.claim: The row attaches a 3-verse digit to a quoted spelling that stands in exactly one verse, silently blending two unnamed attested spellings, and it states the motto's framing relation backwards against the bytes.
items.evidence: The quoted formula אָמַ֣ר קֹהֶ֔לֶת (oshb:Eccl.1.2, byte tier) occurs as a contiguous consonantal run in exactly 1 verse book-wide (skeleton sweep: 1 verse, Eccl.1.2). Reaching 3 requires blending two further attested spellings the row never names: the FEMININE אָמְרָ֖ה קֹהֶ֑לֶת (oshb:Eccl.7.27, byte tier) and the plene-definite אָמַ֥ר הַקּוֹהֶ֖לֶת (oshb:Eccl.12.8, byte tier). The same trap sits one layer down: defective qohelet returns 6 verses (Eccl.1.1, 1:2, 1:12, 7:27, 12:9, 12:10) -- the seventh site is 12:8's plene form, which escapes that spelling sweep entirely. Semantic-class count discipline requires the swept object (spelling vs formula class) to be named before the digit; the row names neither and cites the 3-verse figure immediately after a masculine defective quotation. Second defect, byte-grounded: MT 1:2 runs hevel-havalim / amar-qohelet / hevel-havalim ha-kol hevel, so the said-formula is verse-MEDIAL and is bracketed BY the two superlative doublings; the row's 'framed by the said-qohelet formula' inverts that relation, and it is load-bearing because the row's frame_narration verdict over wisdom_poem rests precisely on the formula's framing function. Byte-true and correctly handled: the superlative doubling does stand twice in MT 1:2, all three quoted runs re-collate at byte tier, and the far-end plene counterpart is gestured at without a bare coordinate.

items.claim: The four-image series is enumerated out of byte order, and the row's 'internal bracket' framing of the under-the-sun refrain conceals its third chapter-1 member sitting past the row's own closing seam.
items.evidence: Series ordinals do not byte-settle. The bytes run דּ֤וֹר הֹלֵךְ֙ וְד֣וֹר בָּ֔א (oshb:Eccl.1.4, byte tier), וְזָרַ֥ח הַשֶּׁ֖מֶשׁ (oshb:Eccl.1.5, byte tier), הוֹלֵ֣ךְ הָר֔וּחַ (oshb:Eccl.1.6, byte tier), כָּל הַנְּחָלִים֙ (oshb:Eccl.1.7, byte tier) -- generations, sun, wind, rivers -- while the row enumerates 'sun, wind, rivers, generations'. Under tier/ordinal discipline the series settles from the bytes first. Second: tachat-hashemesh is attested in 27 verses book-wide, of which chapter 1 holds 3 -- Eccl.1.3, 1:9 and 1:14. The device note calls the 1:3/1:9 pair 'a refrain bracket internal to this row' and does not disclose the third member at 1:14, which stands past the row's own 1:11/1:12 closing seam; a byte-true refrain resuming immediately across a seam argues continuity against the row unless disclosed, and calling the pair a closed internal bracket is exactly the disclosure the row owed. The near-seam texture is denser still: 1:13 carries tachat-ha-shamayim, a different formula on a near-identical skeleton (skeleton sweep: 3 verses -- 1:13, 2:3, 3:1). Third: 'no first-person marker or vocative restart anywhere inside it' is a universal with no digit beside it, and it is contested at the byte level by מִלְּפָנֵֽנוּ (oshb:Eccl.1.10, byte tier), a 1cp suffix and the poem's one first-person form. The defensible version of the claim is byte-true and should be the one stated: standalone ani is absent from every verse of 1:3-1:11, checked verse by verse against the consonantal index. Handled cleanly and worth recording: the petuchah citation matches pmarks_Eccl.json at MT Eccl.1.11 under the correct TYPE (PE, not conflated with the 3 SAMEKH), single-witness and tier-3 are both stated, and it is cited as coincidence rather than as a boundary driver.

items.claim: The row's sole boundary warrant -- dibbarti versus natati -- is falsified by the bytes one verse inside its own span, and the dibbarti form is attested at only one other site, where it opens nothing.
items.evidence: The row separates 1:16-18 from the preceding unit on the claim that 1:16's דִּבַּ֨רְתִּי אֲנִ֤י עִם לִבִּי֙ (oshb:Eccl.1.16, byte tier) is a restart distinct from the natati verb of 1:13. The bytes contest this from inside the row's own span: MT 1:17 reads וָאֶתְּנָ֤ה לִבִּי֙ לָדַ֣עַת (oshb:Eccl.1.17, byte tier) -- the same natan-plus-lev-plus-lamed-infinitive-of-cognition construction as 1:13's וְנָתַ֣תִּי אֶת לִבִּ֗י לִדְר֤וֹשׁ וְלָתוּר֙ (oshb:Eccl.1.13, byte tier). Both witnesses render the pair identically ('I applied my heart to seek and to search out by wisdom' web:Eccl.1.13; 'I applied my heart to know wisdom' web:Eccl.1.17), so this is not a rendering artifact in either direction. The claimed discriminator therefore straddles the very seam it is offered to cut, which under cross-seam cohesion argues continuity against the row unless disclosed -- and it is not disclosed. The digit compounds it: dibbarti is attested in exactly 2 verses book-wide (skeleton sweep: 2 verses, Eccl.1.16 and Eccl.2.15), and at MT 2:15 it stands verse-MEDIAL as וְדִבַּ֣רְתִּי בְלִבִּ֔י (oshb:Eccl.2.15, byte tier), opening nothing; a two-site form whose other site is boundary-irrelevant cannot carry a unit-opening warrant by itself. The lexical field is shared rather than distinctive: libbi occurs in 14 verses, and 1:13, 1:16, 1:17, 2:1, 2:3 and 2:15 form an unbroken heart-formula chain running straight through every seam this cluster cuts. Secondary defect: the rejected_alternative names the tooling inside row prose ('which the toolkit's frame-spine sweep tracks'), which the register rules forbid. Byte-true and correctly stated: the quoted run reaches byte tier, and the device note that the row carries no hevel token holds -- the bare token stands in 30 verses, none of them 1:16, 1:17 or 1:18.

items.claim: The amarti opener does not discriminate a boundary: it occurs twice inside this two-verse row, recurs verse-initially inside a neighbouring row where it opens nothing, and shares its be-libbi idiom with the very verse it is said to be distinct from.
items.evidence: 2:1's אָמַ֤רְתִּֽי אֲנִי֙ בְּלִבִּ֔י (oshb:Eccl.2.1, byte tier) is followed immediately by לִשְׂח֖וֹק אָמַ֣רְתִּי (oshb:Eccl.2.2, byte tier) -- a second amarti token inside the row's own two verses (skeleton sweep amarti: 9 verses, and both 2:1 and 2:2 are members). A form appearing twice in a two-verse row cannot by itself mark that row's opening. The three-token formula amarti-ani-be-libbi is attested in 4 verses (Eccl.2.1, 2:15, 3:17, 3:18); at MT 2:15 it stands VERSE-INITIAL as וְאָמַ֨רְתִּֽי אֲנִ֜י בְּלִבִּ֗י (oshb:Eccl.2.15, byte tier -- accent_stripped-identical to 2:1 apart from the prefixed waw) and opens no row, sitting mid-unit inside the neighbouring row of this same cluster. Third, the rejected_alternative rests on 2:3 pivoting under a new heart-formula, but 2:3 reads תַּ֣רְתִּי בְלִבִּ֔י (oshb:Eccl.2.3, byte tier): be-libbi occurs in 5 verses (2:1, 2:3, 2:15, 3:17, 3:18), so 2:1 and 2:3 share the identical prepositional idiom -- shared-token continuity across the row's own closing seam, undisclosed, with the formula 'new' only in its verb. Fourth, the device note's parenthetical (that 1:2's occurrences belong to the frame motto, outside this row) implies the only prior hevel is the frame's, but the bare token already stands inside the monologue at MT 1:14, הַכֹּ֛ל הֶ֖בֶל (oshb:Eccl.1.14, byte tier) -- and this row's own parent collection begins at 1:12, so 1:14 is monologue-internal. Byte-true: the quoted run reaches byte tier and 2:1 does close on a bare hevel token.

items.claim: The rejected_alternative's syntactic warrant is byte-false -- MT 2:4 opens asyndetically with a finite verb, so a clause break stands exactly where the row asserts none.
items.evidence: The row rejects splitting the works catalogue from its 2:3 introduction because 2:3's purpose clause 'syntactically governs the project the following verses enumerate, with no clause break between them.' The bytes refute the stated warrant: 2:3's subordinate clause is עַ֣ד אֲשֶׁר אֶרְאֶ֗ה (oshb:Eccl.2.3, byte tier), 2:3 closes its own sentence at מִסְפַּ֖ר יְמֵ֥י חַיֵּיהֶֽם (oshb:Eccl.2.3, byte tier), and 2:4 opens הִגְדַּ֖לְתִּי מַעֲשָׂ֑י (oshb:Eccl.2.4, byte tier) -- a finite 1cs verb with no conjunction at all. Asyndeton is a clause break, and the strongest one available in this register; whatever hold 2:3 has over 2:4-2:8 is semantic, not syntactic continuity, so the warrant has to be replaced rather than restated. The row also leaves its genuinely byte-true binder unclaimed: the ethical dative li runs at 2:4, 2:5, 2:6, 2:7, 2:8 and 2:9 (6 consecutive verses), and the phrase mi-kol she-hayah/she-hayu le-fanay bi-yerushalaim recurs at 2:7 and 2:9 -- real cohesion evidence, stronger than the syntax claim it would replace. Second: the device note's 'fixed et-plus-infinitive register template of the time list at 3:1-8' overstates its range. MT 3:1 reads לַכֹּ֖ל זְמָ֑ן וְעֵ֥ת (oshb:Eccl.3.1, byte tier), whose et is followed by לְכָל חֵ֖פֶץ (oshb:Eccl.3.1, byte tier), not by an infinitive; the et-plus-lamed-infinitive template begins at 3:2 with עֵ֥ת לָלֶ֖דֶת (oshb:Eccl.3.2, byte tier). Third: the root claim is byte-defensible but mislabeled -- תַּ֣רְתִּי בְלִבִּ֔י (oshb:Eccl.2.3) and 1:13's לִדְר֤וֹשׁ וְלָתוּר֙ (oshb:Eccl.1.13) do share the root tur, yet '(natan/tur versus tarti)' pairs a finite verb and an infinitive drawn from the same verse 1:13 against 2:3's finite form, so the contrast as written does not name what actually differs. Byte-true and correctly stated: no standalone ani stands anywhere in 2:4-2:8 (ch-2 ani sites: 2:1, 2:11, 2:12, 2:13, 2:14, 2:15, 2:18, 2:20, 2:24 -- 9 verses, none inside 2:4-2:10).

items.claim: The verdict device this row cites as its own evidence recurs one verse past its closing seam at consonantally identical strength, and the straddle is undisclosed while a much smaller internal repetition is disclosed.
items.evidence: The row lists the hevel and reut-ruach refrains among its substrate signals on the strength of 2:11's הַכֹּ֥ל הֶ֨בֶל֙ וּרְע֣וּת ר֔וּחַ (oshb:Eccl.2.11, byte tier). That 4-token run is attested in exactly 3 verses book-wide (skeleton sweep: 3 verses -- Eccl.1.14, 2:11, 2:17), and MT 2:17, the FIRST verse past this row's 2:16/2:17 boundary, carries הַכֹּ֥ל הֶ֖בֶל וּרְע֥וּת רֽוּחַ (oshb:Eccl.2.17, byte tier) -- accent_stripped-identical to the 1:14 occurrence and skeleton-identical to 2:11's. The under-the-sun refrain compounds it: tachat-hashemesh stands at 2:11 inside the row, is absent from 2:12-2:16, then resumes unbroken at 2:17, 2:18, 2:19 and 2:20 immediately outside it (sweep: 27 verses book-wide). A byte-true device straddling the row's own seam argues continuity against the row unless disclosed; this row discloses its internal 2:11/2:12 repetition and says nothing about the far denser recurrence across its lower boundary -- and reut-ruach is itself only a 7-verse refrain (1:14, 2:11, 2:17, 2:26, 4:4, 4:6, 6:9) whose two nearest members sit on opposite sides of that seam. Second, undisclosed inside the span: MT 2:15 opens וְאָמַ֨רְתִּֽי אֲנִ֜י בְּלִבִּ֗י (oshb:Eccl.2.15, byte tier), the same verse-initial formula a neighbouring row of this cluster treats as a unit-opening driver at 2:1; the two rows cannot be read consistently without that disclosure. Credit where the bytes give it, and verified: u-faniti is attested in exactly 2 verses book-wide (Eccl.2.11 and 2:12) -- וּפָנִ֣יתִֽי אֲנִ֗י (oshb:Eccl.2.11, byte tier) -- the two runs differ only in cantillation (accent_stripped-identical, so the row's 'skeleton-level' label is conservative rather than overstated), each was spliced from its own verse's pointed bytes, and both re-collate at byte tier; this is the cluster's cleanest tier handling.
